story.head: Where the Islanders have the edge: depth
paras: The Jets (10-9-3) lost 2-1 to Ottawa on Tuesday. The Islanders have won three straight, the last a 5-1 rout of Columbus. Going in, the Isles are fourth in the Metropolitan (16th in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 17th).
The Islanders’ record (.600) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Jets’ record (.523) is about what their chances are worth.

The Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Islanders have the edge over the Jets on depth. As for the Jets, they create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd), rarely ice the puck (4th) and get their shots through to the net (5th).

Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Islanders in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games. Kyle Connor (17 G / 9 A / 26 P in 22 GP) is tied for the Jets’ scoring lead, with seven points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (7 G / 19 A / 26 P in 22 GP) shares it, with ten points in his last five games.
Semyon Varlamov (2-2-2 / .898 SV% in 6 GS) is expected to start for the Islanders, and Stuart Skinner (7-5-3 / .883 SV% in 16 GS) for Winnipeg.
At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Koepke, Barron and Zhilkin out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Duclair, Cizikas and Chaffee.
